Pre-train the encoder from a peak catalog (smoke test only)

Source: R/pretrain.R
pretrain_autoencoder_from_catalog.Rd

Same idea as pretrain_autoencoder() but generates the synthetic pretraining set via generate_one_synthetic_from_catalog(). Use this when you have a catalog (perhaps loaded from disk) but not the original peak_params object.

Usage

pretrain_autoencoder_from_catalog(
  catalog,
  H,
  W,
  n_synthetic = 2000L,
  epochs = 30L,
  batch_size = 32L,
  lr = 0.001,
  weight_decay = 1e-04,
  add_noise = TRUE,
  stem_stride_rt = 4L,
  stem_stride_cv = 1L,
  device = if (torch::cuda_is_available()) "cuda" else "cpu",
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

catalog

A peak_catalog object.

H, W

Synthetic image dimensions.

n_synthetic

Number of synthetic samples to generate.

epochs, batch_size, lr, weight_decay

Optimization parameters.

add_noise

If TRUE, denoising autoencoder; if FALSE, reconstruction.

stem_stride_rt, stem_stride_cv

Encoder stem strides.

device

"cpu" or "cuda".

seed

RNG seed.

Value

List with encoder, autoencoder, loss_history.

Details

For real pretraining runs prefer pretrain_denoising_online() with catalog = your_catalog — that generates fresh batches per training step, so the model can see effectively unlimited unique synthetic samples with constant memory. This pre-alloc version holds the full n_synthetic × H × W tensor in RAM and reuses the same set every epoch, which caps the effective training data. It stays available for smoke tests (n_synthetic <= a few thousand).
